summary: The proposal is well-structured, clearly written, and covers all required sections with appropriate depth. The problem/motivation/objective logic is coherent, the two figures are well-captioned and referenced, and the AI transparency statement is specific about tools. However, it falls short on two critical/major points: the bibliography has only 5 references (minimum 6) and the schedule contains a date inconsistency plus a forbidden documentation task. Addressing these three issues and the minor sentence-start violations would bring the proposal to a submittable state.

findings.title: Bibliography contains only 5 references (minimum 6 required)
findings.description: The bibliography lists 5 publications ([TP21], [AAM17], [BBE10], [Bog+07], [NM06]). The guidelines require at least 6–8 peer-reviewed publications. The student must add at least one additional peer-reviewed source (e.g., a paper on LLM-based feedback generation, prompt engineering, or agentic LLM architectures) to meet the minimum threshold.

locations.quote: [TP21] T. Tuononen and A. Parpala … [AAM17] P. Ashwin … [BBE10] J. Bitchener … [Bog+07] M. Bogo … [NM06] D. J. Nicol and D. Macfarlane-Dick …

findings.title: Schedule start date inconsistent with first iteration date
findings.description: The title page and schedule text state the thesis starts on 26.06.2026, but Iteration 1 is dated 08.06.2026 — 18 days before the stated start. The iteration dates (08.06 → 26.10) span exactly 20 weeks and are internally consistent, so either the start date on the title page/schedule text is wrong or the iteration dates need to be shifted. The student must reconcile these so the first iteration begins on or after the official start date.

locations.quote: The Bachelor thesis starts on **26.06.2026** … Iteration 1 (**08.06.2026** - 2 weeks)

findings.title: Iteration 9 includes a documentation task
findings.description: Iteration 9 lists 'Documentation' as a work item. The guidelines explicitly state that the schedule must not include thesis writing, documentation writing, or presentation preparation tasks. Additionally, 'Review the system and check for bugs' is vague and not a measurable deliverable. Replace with a concrete, measurable engineering task (e.g., 'Run end-to-end integration tests covering all four objectives and fix identified defects').

locations.quote: Iteration 9 (05.10.2026 - 3 weeks) • Review the system and check for bugs • **Documentation**

findings.title: Three sentences begin with forbidden words (As, Since, Because)
findings.description: The guidelines prohibit sentences starting with 'As…', 'Since…', or 'Because…'. Three instances were found: (1) 'As Figure 1 illustrates…' in Motivation, (2) 'Since guidelines may not already be in a suitable format…' in Objective 4.1, (3) 'Because the feedback tool is powered by LLMs…' in the Motivation/4.1 boundary. Rephrase each sentence to avoid the forbidden opener (e.g., 'Figure 1 illustrates…', 'Guidelines may not yet be in a suitable format, so…', 'The feedback tool is powered by LLMs, enabling students to…').

locations.quote: **As** Figure 1 illustrates, an LLM-powered Reviewer works alongside the supervisor, evaluating the thesis against the research group's writing guidelines
**Since** guidelines may not already be in a suitable format, the LLM may first need to preprocess them into a structured representation it can act on.
**Because** the feedback tool is powered by LLMs, students can obtain instant formative feedback at any point during the writing process.

findings.title: Inconsistent terminology for the core system concept
findings.description: The same system is referred to as 'the tool' (Abstract), 'an LLM-powered Reviewer' (Motivation, tied to Figure 1), 'the LLM' (4.1), and 'the feedback tool' (4.2–4.4). While 'LLM-powered Reviewer' is the label used in Figure 1, the main body should settle on one consistent term (e.g., 'the feedback tool' or 'the Reviewer') after the initial introduction. The current switching may confuse readers about whether these are distinct entities.

locations.quote: an **LLM-powered Reviewer** works alongside the supervisor
When **the feedback tool** has access to previous iterations
**the LLM** may first need to preprocess them

findings.title: AI transparency statement lacks section-specific detail
findings.description: The transparency statement lists tools and general purposes (grammar, translation, content generation, coding, citations) but does not specify which sections of the proposal each tool was applied to. The guidelines expect the statement to mention 'which sections of the proposal the AI tools were used for.' Add a brief mapping, e.g., 'Grammarly was used primarily on the Problem and Motivation sections; GitHub Copilot assisted with Typst macros for the figure generation in Section 4.'

locations.section: Transparency in the Use of AI Tools
locations.quote: In preparing this proposal, I made use of several AI-based tools **across different stages of the writing process**.
